_comment: Wall-clock seconds for one bats file in its own bats call on a GitHub windows-latest runner, Node 20. Used ONLY to balance CI shards -- never to gate anything. Stale numbers cost balance, never correctness: shard-tests.mjs asserts every file lands in exactly one shard whether or not it appears here.
_why: arc-ci's windows leg costs 1585s against ~145s on ubuntu for the same 563 tests -- 2.82s per test against 0.26s, because every bats `run` spawns a process and windows process creation is dear. Measured 2026-07-31 (run 30611012771): excluding the workspace and bats' binaries from Microsoft Defender changes nothing, because the runner image already ships with realtime protection OFF and both drives excluded. There is no windows-side saving left to find, so the fix stays splitting.
_provenance: 119 of 119 discovered files re-measured in a single pass on 2026-08-13 (run 31683960460, weigh-tests.yml, on feat/arc-bench-phase-00-rest) -- one file per job on windows-latest, each timed in its own bats call with the scanners arc-ci installs, the same method as every earlier pass. Re-run that workflow and paste its block rather than editing numbers by hand. The previous pass (2026-08-12, run 31627029442) measured 112 of 115 and had to exclude three; this one measured EVERY file and excluded none.
_evidence: The 2026-08-10 pass measured 104 files, 44 of which had NO entry at all and were riding _default_weight 16. The two this slice grew were among them and wrong in the same direction by roughly sevenfold: leads-journey.bats 111s and leads-mail-guard.bats 120s. (An earlier version of this sentence said 47 covered; 47 was the count MISSING before the run, 44 of them were measured, and the other 3 are the ones _known_gap names.) The method is unchanged from the pass that produced the previous table: one file per job on windows, each timed in its own bats call with the scanners arc-ci installs. 2026-08-13: the bench cycle added four files -- bench-core, bench-drift, bench-proposal and bench-seal -- and every one of them was riding _default_weight 16 until this pass. They measured 38s, 32s, 37s and 80s: bench-seal alone was under-weighted FIVEFOLD, because each of these runs a probe that spawns full K=3 bench runs. That is the same shape as the 2026-08-10 gap, one cycle later, and it is why an unmeasured entry has to be visible as a COUNT rather than absorbed into a default.
_floor: spine-emit.bats at 160s is the floor no shard count can beat, and design-steel-thread.bats at 156s is second. Both numbers are from the 2026-08-10 pass; the previous prose here quoted 147s and 128s from the 2026-08-03 pass and was left standing when the table under it was replaced -- a measured claim that stops being re-derived starts lying, which is the whole reason this file records provenance. From 12 shards on, the heaviest shard IS that one file, and one file cannot be split.
_known_gap: NONE. All 119 discovered files measured rc=0 in isolation on windows in this pass, and none was excluded -- the first time that has been true. THE PREVIOUS GAP IS CLOSED: arc-profile.bats, arc-scan.bats and baseline.bats had measured RED in isolation on 2026-08-12 and on main, passing in arc-ci only when sharded alongside arc-tools-image.bats -- an UNDECLARED INTER-FILE DEPENDENCY, so they passed by shard luck and any change to the plan revoked it. The cause was adapters/semgrep.sh ending its scan with `|| true`, so a crashed scanner read as a clean codebase; the bench lane strengthened _arc_need_semgrep to probe the TOOL directly on 2026-08-12 and this pass is the evidence it worked. They now measure 33s, 29s and 17s, standing alone. Keep this field: an unmeasured entry is a DEFAULT rather than an error (retro-log 2026-08-03), so name any new file here rather than letting it disappear.
